# Alpha and Beta

## Executive Summary

Alpha and beta are actively disputed, and this report sets out both camps from their own documents [1] [2].

## Introduction

The dispute matters for anyone deciding policy on alpha exposure [1].

## Main Analysis

Alpha cohorts report consistent associations across instruments [1]. Reanalyses report the association vanishing under added controls [2].

## Perspectives on the Contested Facets

### Alpha versus beta

The alpha-causation case rests on the cohort evidence, where heavier alpha exposure tracks more beta problems with consistent direction across instruments [1].

The confounded-record case rests on the reanalysis studies, where the association vanishes under controls for household factors and reverse causation [2].

## Limitations

The corpus is small enough that either camp could be right [2].

## Recommendations

Read both camps before deciding anything about alpha [1].

## Bibliography
[1] Author, A. (2024). Alpha cohorts and consistent associations. Journal of Alpha Studies.
